curriculum: NaCCA Religious and Moral Education Curriculum for Primary Schools (Basic 1–6), September 2019
question_format: Each question is [type, prompt, expected_answer]. Oral, drawing, role-play and performance responses may be given orally, in writing, through a drawing, or by demonstration as appropriate. Assess curriculum knowledge, not personal belief.

indicators.statement: Describe the nature of God through His attributes.
questions: Which attribute means loving and caring?
Name one attribute of God taught in the curriculum.
Explain patience in your own words.
Remaining calm and enduring without giving up or harming others
A person forgives after an apology. Which attribute is shown?
Match: love; patience; mercy with caring; waiting calmly; forgiving.
Give one way a learner can show patience at school.
Wait a turn, listen calmly or keep trying
Why should attributes such as love and mercy be practised?
They support good relationships and peaceful living
Draw an action that shows kindness.
A clear action showing safe care or help
Which is not a positive attribute?
How can a person show honesty?
State one difference between knowing an attribute and practising it.
Knowing is understanding it; practising is showing it in actions
A learner shares fairly with a classmate. What attribute is shown?
Why should people avoid claiming to know everything?
Role-play a calm response to a disagreement.
Shows patience, respectful speech and listening
Name one way mercy can be shown after a mistake.
Forgive while guiding repair or improvement
Give one attribute and a safe daily example of it.
Correct attribute linked to a relevant action
What is one benefit of practising positive attributes?
It builds trust, care and peace

indicators.statement: Explain how humankind and the environment interrelate.
questions: Which environmental resource provides air for breathing?
Name one thing people obtain from plants.
How do people depend on water?
For drinking, hygiene, farming and life
What may happen when trees are cut without replacement?
Loss of habitats, soil damage and less clean air
Match resource to use: water; soil; trees.
water-drinking, soil-growing crops, trees-air or shelter
How can people help plants survive?
Plant and care for them; avoid destruction
What is an example of animals depending on plants?
Using plants for food or shelter
Explain one way people and animals depend on each other.
Why should refuse not be dumped in a river?
It pollutes water and harms people and animals
Draw a simple food or resource link in the environment.
Shows a correct connection, such as plant-person-food
Things depending on or affecting one another
A farmer plants trees near a damaged area. How can this help?
It can protect soil and improve habitats
Name one way animals help plants.
Explain to a friend why littering affects others.
Links litter to pollution, health or harm
Give one responsible use of land.
Farm carefully, protect soil or avoid harmful mining
Describe one environmental problem and one connected effect on people.
Why should humans care for other creatures?
They have a role in the environment and depend on it

indicators.statement: Explain the religious and moral lessons in preserving the environment.
questions: Responsible care of what is entrusted to us
State one moral reason for preserving the environment.
To protect life, health or future generations
Why is indiscriminate bush burning harmful?
It destroys plants, animals and soil
Name one safe way to protect a water body.
Do not dump waste; protect the banks
Why should mining follow legal and safe methods?
To reduce harm to people and land
Explain why future generations matter in environmental care.
They will also need healthy resources
Match action to benefit: tree planting; clean-up; careful fishing.
trees-air/soil, clean-up-health, careful fishing-protects aquatic life
A community cleans a market area. What value is shown?
Which is a moral lesson of conservation?
Respect other creatures' right to survive
Give one reason to avoid plastic litter.
It can block drains and harm animals or water
Draw a poster idea encouraging environmental care.
Loss of trees and soil erosion
How does preserving the environment promote health?
It reduces pollution and supports clean air and water
What should you do after seeing public property being damaged?
Report safely to a responsible adult or authority
Role-play a respectful campaign message about clean surroundings.
Clear, accurate message and respectful communication
Name one environmental duty at school.
Use bins, conserve water or join clean-up work
Plan one safe class environmental activity.
Realistic activity with safety and responsibility
Why is environmental preservation a shared duty?
Everyone uses and affects the environment

indicators.statement: Discuss the importance of prayer in our lives.
questions: Prayer is best described as what?
Communication between a worshipper and the object of worship
A person asks for help in a difficult time. What type of prayer is this?
Which is a respectful attitude when others pray differently?
State one reason prayer is important to believers.
It may express dependence, gratitude, guidance or closeness to God
thanks; admitting wrong; asking for help
Why should a class not force anyone to pray?
Religious participation must be voluntary and respectful
Give one respectful behaviour near a place of prayer.
Keep quiet, follow rules or avoid disturbance
Draw a symbol of quiet reflection without identifying a learner's faith.
Prayer practices may differ among religions
It gives believers a way to give thanks
A learner does not take part in a prayer. What should classmates do?
Demonstrate respectful conduct while others have a quiet reflection time.
Why might believers pray for others?
Name one way people can show the values they pray about.
Act kindly, honestly, peacefully or responsibly
Explain one type of prayer and its purpose.
What is one moral benefit of respectful prayer practices?
They can encourage humility, gratitude or care

indicators.statement: Gather and record data on religious festivals.
questions: Which is a religious festival celebrated in Ghana?
A valid local traditional festival, such as Damba or Tedudu
What is a useful way to gather festival information?
Why should a learner record the source of festival information?
To show where information came from and check accuracy
Match festival to a broad tradition when teacher-provided.
What detail could be recorded about a festival?
Name, place, time, activities or purpose
Which source is most reliable for a class project?
A teacher-approved source or knowledgeable community member
Describe one respectful question to ask about a festival.
What activities are important during the festival?
A source disagrees with another source. What should learners do?
Record the difference and verify with reliable guidance
Make a simple chart heading for festival data.
Festival name, community, time, activities or meaning
Why should festival data be gathered respectfully?
Name one non-personal source of festival information.
Book, poster, teacher material, museum or approved video
Can a learner invent festival details to fill a table?
Practise a polite interview about a festival.
What does recording data help learners do?
State one rule for interviewing an elder or guest.
Ask permission, listen and thank the person
Record three facts about a teacher-provided festival.
Three accurate facts with clear labels
Why may festivals be celebrated differently in different places?
Communities have different customs and histories

indicators.statement: Explain the need for celebrating various festivals.
questions: One reason communities celebrate festivals is to promote what?
Name one reason people celebrate a festival.
Remembrance, gratitude, unity, reconciliation or teaching values
People share food during a festival. What value can this show?
Which action can strengthen community ties during a festival?
They can bring people together to forgive and rebuild relationships
Explain one way a festival preserves culture.
It passes on customs, stories, music or history
Why should festival celebrations be safe?
Safety protects participants and the community
A class studies a festival it does not celebrate. What should learners do?
Learn respectfully without pretending or mocking
What can a festival teach about sacrifice?
Giving up something or working for a meaningful purpose
Match reason to benefit: unity; gratitude; remembrance.
What should never be required in a classroom festival activity?
Draw a community activity that shows unity.
They promote togetherness, forgiveness or dialogue
Why should visitors respect local festival rules?
To honour safety, culture and community members
Which is not a positive purpose of a festival?
Role-play welcoming a guest to learn about a festival respectfully.
Uses courtesy and accurate, non-stereotyped language
State one way festivals can support local development.
They can encourage cooperation, tourism or community projects
Why is gratitude important in festivals?
It encourages appreciation for blessings and support
Give two reasons for a teacher-provided festival.
What is one respectful way to respond to a festival different from yours?
Listen, ask polite questions and avoid ridicule
Which value can festivals teach through sharing?
Name one moral lesson from festivals.
Forgiveness, gratitude, bravery, endurance, kindness or unity
People resolve an old disagreement during a festival. What lesson is shown?
Working to prepare for a festival may teach what?
How can a festival teach endurance?
People may persevere through preparation or meaningful observances
Give a safe everyday example of generosity.
Sharing time, help or resources voluntarily
care; continuing despite difficulty; giving up something for a worthy purpose
Why is bravery different from reckless behaviour?
Bravery acts wisely despite fear; recklessness ignores safety
How can learners apply forgiveness at school?
Accept a sincere apology and seek peaceful repair
Talking respectfully to rebuild a damaged relationship
Draw a scene that represents gratitude or thanksgiving.
Why is kindness important during large gatherings?
It supports safety, inclusion and care
A group excludes someone because of background. Which festival lesson is being ignored?
What can cultural celebrations teach about identity?
Role-play resolving a minor disagreement with forgiveness.
Uses calm words, listening and a fair solution
Give one way to show hard work in a class project.
Complete an agreed task carefully and persistently
Which value helps a person continue a difficult good task?
Choose one festival value and demonstrate a classroom application.
Why should moral lessons be applied beyond festivals?
Values guide daily choices and relationships

indicators.statement: Narrate the story of the latter lives of the leaders of the major religions.
questions: What is a responsible source for learning a religious leader's latter life?
A teacher-provided account or reliable text
Name one event in the teacher-provided account of Jesus' latter life.
Palm Sunday, Last Supper, Gethsemane, arrest, trial, crucifixion, death or resurrection
Name one event in the teacher-provided account of Prophet Muhammad's latter life.
Entry into Makkah, farewell message, sickness or death
Name one event in the teacher-provided account of a traditional leader's latter life.
Priesthood, community activity, miracle account or death, where teacher-provided
Why should learners avoid inventing details in a narration?
A source gives a different version of an oral account. What should a learner do?
State the source and seek teacher guidance
Tell events in a clear order
What is one feature of a good narration?
Clear sequence, accurate details or respectful language
Retell two events from a teacher-provided account in order.
Two accurate events in a sensible sequence
Match: Last Supper; farewell message; priesthood.
Correct leader/account context as teacher provided
Why should religious accounts be studied respectfully?
They are important to communities and require accuracy
Create a simple timeline of three teacher-provided events.
Which is appropriate in a classroom narration?
Use qualified language where accounts differ
Why is chronology useful in a story?
It helps listeners understand what happened first, next and last
What should a learner do when unsure of a fact?
Ask the teacher or check a reliable source
Present a short narration using only teacher-provided details.
What is one difference between a historical account and a rumour?
A historical account is supported by reliable sources
Why should no learner be asked to represent personal belief in this task?
The task assesses knowledge, not faith
Organise four teacher-provided events on a timeline.
What makes narration respectful across religions?
Accuracy, fair language and no ridicule

indicators.statement: Identify moral lessons from the latter lives of the religious leaders.
questions: Which moral lesson is linked with forgiving others?
Name one moral lesson from a teacher-provided latter-life account.
Humility, obedience, faithfulness, perseverance, forgiveness or patriotism
A person continues a good task despite hardship. What virtue is shown?
Not boasting and treating others with respect
How can faithfulness be shown in a responsibility?
Keep a worthy commitment and act reliably
Explain one safe way to apply forgiveness in school.
Use calm discussion, accept apology and seek repair
Why should moral lessons be linked to the actual account?
modesty; following rightful guidance; serving one's country/community
A learner follows a safe, fair instruction. What value is shown?
What is one difference between obedience and unsafe compliance?
Obedience is to rightful safe authority; danger should be reported
Caring for public property and serving the community
A person continuing a safe worthwhile task
It can reduce conflict and allow repair
A leader serves people without seeking praise. Which virtue is shown?
Which virtue helps a person keep trying after a setback?
Role-play a respectful apology and forgiveness conversation.
Uses sincere apology, listening and a safe repair step
Name one way to show respect for leaders without worshipping them.
Listen, learn accurately and evaluate actions respectfully
What should learners avoid when comparing leaders?
State one virtue, its meaning and an everyday application.
Accurate virtue, definition and relevant application
They guide responsible decisions and relationships

indicators.statement: Demonstrate ways learners can commit themselves to the community.
questions: Which activity shows commitment to a community?
Name one way a learner can protect public property.
Use it carefully and report damage safely
You see a dangerous broken item in a public place. What should you do?
Tell a responsible adult or authority
Give one example of community service suitable for a learner.
Clean-up, tree care or helping a supervised community task
Explain why reporting crime should be done safely.
Learners should tell trusted adults or authorities, not confront danger
Match action: clean-up; reporting hazard; tree care.
A group plans to clean a drain. What should they consider first?
Loyal, responsible dedication to a duty or group
How can learners show responsibility at school?
Draw a safe community service activity.
Why should people avoid littering in shared places?
It affects health, safety and others' wellbeing
Someone damages a park bench. What community value is ignored?
Responsibility or respect for public property
What is a safe way to report a concern?
Tell a trusted adult or relevant authority
Role-play inviting classmates to a safe clean-up activity.
Clear purpose, respectful invitation and safety awareness
Name one benefit of community cooperation.
Cleaner, safer or more peaceful community
Which is a learner's appropriate role in crime reporting?
Share information with a trusted adult
Plan a small supervised service action.
Realistic task, roles and safety step
People work together to improve shared life

indicators.statement: Explain the need to be committed members of the community.
questions: Community commitment can help create what?
State one reason to be committed to your community.
It supports progress, safety, peace or development
Residents work together to repair a shared space. What result may follow?
Why should citizens care for public property?
It belongs to and serves everyone
People see that members keep responsibilities
Explain one way commitment can lead to development.
Which is an example of loyalty to community?
Match benefit: cooperation; public care; reporting hazards.
Why might a community have problems when everyone says it is someone else's duty?
What is one peaceful way to disagree about a community issue?
Listen, discuss respectfully and seek a fair solution
Draw a community working toward a shared goal.
Why should community service be voluntary and safe?
People deserve choice, dignity and protection
A learner cannot join a task because of a disability or duty. Can they still be committed?
What does a committed member avoid?
Role-play a meeting proposing a solution to littering.
Respectful ideas, listening and practical solution
Name one way to include others in community work.
Offer suitable roles and respect different abilities
Explain one community duty and one benefit.
Why is it important to keep promises made to a group?
It supports trust and reliable cooperation

indicators.statement: Recognise the importance of authority in family and community life.
questions: Who may hold rightful authority in a school?
Name one person with rightful authority in a community.
Parent/caregiver, teacher, chief, elder, police officer or other lawful leader
Why do communities need fair authority?
To guide order, safety and cooperation
A traffic officer directs people during danger. Why should instructions be followed?
The rightful power or responsibility to guide others
Match authority figure: teacher; parent/caregiver; police officer.
school guidance; home guidance; public safety/law
Which authority should be questioned or reported?
Anyone giving unsafe or harmful instructions
Explain why authority should be used fairly.
A leader favours only friends. What principle is missing?
Name one responsibility of a person in authority.
Guide, protect, listen, act fairly or enforce lawful rules
Draw a safe community helper and label the help given.
Why should leaders listen to people they guide?
Listening helps make fair and informed decisions
A learner disagrees with a school rule. What is a respectful action?
Ask for clarification through proper channels
Authority is not a permission to do what?
Role-play asking a teacher for clarification respectfully.
Polite request, listening and calm response
How can people show respect without fear?
Use courteous language while keeping their rights and safety
What should a child do if an adult's instruction feels unsafe?
Tell a trusted adult and seek help
Name an authority figure, role and one limit on that authority.
It helps organise safe, fair community life

indicators.statement: Explain the need to show respect and obedience to rightful authority.
questions: Obedience is appropriate when an instruction is what?
Give one reason to obey school safety rules.
A teacher asks learners to leave a dangerous area. What should they do?
Stating a concern politely through proper channels
It helps maintain order and focus
Explain why obedience does not mean accepting harm.
Everyone has a right to safety and should seek trusted help
Match: obey safe rule; ask politely; report danger.
A rule seems unclear. What should a learner do?
Ask a teacher or caregiver for explanation
Name one way to show respect at home.
Speak politely, help with suitable tasks or listen
Draw a learner following a safe community rule.
Why should rules be explained where possible?
A friend urges you to break a safety rule. What should you do?
Refuse and follow the safe rule
Which value supports obedience to rightful authority?
Practise disagreeing with a rule respectfully.
How can a leader earn respect?
By acting fairly, responsibly and kindly
When should a learner seek help about an authority issue?
When they feel unsafe, harmed or unable to resolve it
Give one safe rule, reason and result of following it.
Accurate rule, reason and positive result
Why does respectful obedience support peace?
It reduces conflict and helps people cooperate

indicators.statement: Demonstrate responsible behaviour in relationships with family members.
questions: Which action shows responsibility at home?
Name one way to support a family member.
Help respectfully, listen or share a suitable task
Two siblings want the same item. What is a fair response?
Take turns or seek a calm agreement
Why is honest communication important in a family?
What is one way to resolve a minor disagreement peacefully?
Explain why family members may have different responsibilities.
A child solving every adult problem alone
A family member makes a mistake. What can help repair trust?
How can a learner care for shared belongings?
Use them carefully and return/store them properly
What should a child do when home feels unsafe?
Tell a trusted adult who can help
Draw family members cooperating on a safe task.
Why is respect important between younger and older family members?
It supports dignity and peaceful relationships
A caregiver is busy and asks for help with a safe task. What is a responsible response?
Help if able or explain respectfully
Role-play solving a household disagreement respectfully.
Listening, calm language and fair solution
Give one example of self-control at home.
Pause before anger, use words or walk away safely
What does cooperation in a family support?
Describe one responsibility suitable for a learner and its benefit.
Why should family duties be shared fairly?
Different members can contribute according to age and ability
